titulo: News and media: The language of the news

aula.objetivo: Read and understand the style of a news story and a headline, report what other people said, and talk about news, social media and hoaxes with the right vocabulary and structures.

itens.pt: the news story, a piece of news

blocos.titulo: How a news story is written
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: a news story has fixed parts: the «titular» (headline), the subtitle, the «entradilla» (the lead, the first paragraph that sums everything up) and the «cuerpo» (the body). STEP 2: the lead answers five questions: ¿qué ocurrió?, ¿quién?, ¿dónde?, ¿cuándo? and ¿por qué? — the same "five Ws" as in English journalism. If you can answer all five, you've got the gist. STEP 3: headlines have their own style. Like English headlines, they use the present for past events and drop articles and auxiliaries: «Un incendio destruye una nave industrial» (Fire destroys warehouse) — more common in headlines than «Un incendio ha destruido…». STEP 4: in the body, the main event usually comes in the preterite (lesson 19): «El fuego comenzó a las ocho.» For something very recent, linked to the present, the present perfect appears: «Los bomberos han controlado el incendio.» STEP 5: with markers of finished past time (ayer, el lunes, la semana pasada) use the preterite: «Ayer inauguraron la biblioteca.» STEP 6: the passive and «se» (lesson 49) are frequent: «La biblioteca fue inaugurada ayer.», «Se investigan las causas.» (The causes are being investigated.) STEP 7: words: «periódico» and «diario» are the newspaper («diario» is also a personal diary); «papel» is paper as a material, never the newspaper. «Telediario» is the TV news in Spain. And "a piece of news" is simply «una noticia»; "the news" (in general) is «las noticias».
blocos.comparacao: English "the news" is uncountable; in Spanish «noticia» is countable: «una noticia» (a piece of news), «las noticias» (the news). "The paper" is «el periódico», not «el papel». "According to the police" is «según la policía», with no preposition. And "fake news" is «bulo» (Spain) or «noticia falsa» (common in Latin America too).

tabela.funcao: answers: what, who, where, when, why
tabela.exemplo: El ayuntamiento inauguró ayer una biblioteca…

erros.errado: Un incendio ha destruido ayer una nave.
erros.certo: Un incendio destruyó ayer una nave.
erros.motivo: With «ayer» (finished past), the preterite is the right tense.

erros.errado: Leí la noticia en el papel.
erros.certo: Leí la noticia en el periódico.
erros.motivo: "The paper" is «el periódico»; «papel» is only the material.

erros.errado: Un incendio destruiría una nave. (headline for a confirmed event)
erros.motivo: The conditional in a headline signals a rumour, not a confirmed fact.

blocos.enunciado: Make up a short headline about a neighbourhood event (a fair, roadworks, a match). Then say in three sentences what happened, where and when.
Say out loud how you'd tell someone about something you did yesterday and something you did today (preterite and present perfect), and explain why the form changes with the time marker.
